Frederick stared at the glowing runes, the weight of eternity pressing against his chest. The draft intensified, tearing a page from the ancient book. Instead of reaching for the vial of shimmering liquid he had prepared, he grabbed the parchment. He realized that eternal life was not a gift, but a cage—a static existence devoid of the very urgency that gave life meaning. With a trembling hand, he struck a match and held it to the corner of the page. As the fire consumed the secrets of immortality, he felt a profound sense of peace. He turned and walked out of the hidden chamber, leaving the altar empty and the secret lost to time, choosing the beauty of a finite life over the horror of endless days.

The explorer who reached America in 1492 is Christopher Columbus.
